title: Visual Process Breakdown Generator
use_case: Create simple step-by-step visual process explanations
description: Generates clean visual instructions that break a process into simple, easy-to-follow steps.
body:
Break down [PROCESS] into 4–6 simple visual steps.

Requirements:
- Each step should be immediately understandable at a glance.
- Use minimal text.
- Prioritize visual clarity over decoration.
- Keep the composition clean and organized.
- Use consistent icons, colors, and layout across all steps.
- Make each step visually distinct.
- Include arrows, spacing, or visual flow indicators where helpful.
- Avoid clutter and unnecessary details.
- Design in a modern infographic style.
- Ensure the final output is readable on both desktop and mobile.

title: Simple Visual Topic Explainer
use_case: Explain complex topics in an extremely simple way
description: Helps simplify difficult concepts using plain language, visual metaphors, and beginner-friendly explanations.
body:
Explain [TOPIC] in the simplest possible way.

Requirements:
- Assume I have absolutely no prior knowledge.
- Use plain, everyday language.
- Avoid jargon unless absolutely necessary.
- If a technical term must be used, explain it immediately in simple words.
- Use visual metaphors, analogies, or simple imaginary illustrations to make concepts intuitive.
- Break the explanation into small, easy-to-follow sections.
- Prioritize clarity over completeness.
- Make the explanation feel conversational and beginner-friendly.
- Use examples from daily life whenever possible.
- End with a short one-sentence summary that captures the core idea.

title: Copyright-Safe Learning Video Architect
use_case: Transform book ideas into original educational video concepts
description: Creates fully original educational video structures inspired by underlying ideas from a source without reproducing copyrighted material.
body:
You are an expert Learning Designer, Visual Story Architect, and Copyright-Safe Educator.

SOURCE CONTEXT (DO NOT QUOTE OR REPRODUCE):
I have studied a chapter from a book. You must NOT:
- quote the text
- reproduce examples, metaphors, diagrams, tables, or structure from the chapter
- follow the chapter’s order or logic
- mention the book or author
- create content that could replace reading the chapter

YOUR TASK:
Create an ORIGINAL educational video inspired by the underlying IDEAS only.

TRANSFORMATION RULES (MANDATORY):
1. Abstract ideas into general principles, mental models, or skills.
2. Recompose the content using a NEW structure unrelated to the chapter.
3. Invent NEW examples, metaphors, and visuals.
4. Add interpretation, synthesis, or application that is not present in the chapter.
5. Ensure the result stands alone as independent knowledge.

OUTPUT FORMAT (VIDEO-READY):

1. VIDEO THEME
- One sentence describing the core idea, phrased generically.

2. CORE CONCEPTS (3–5)
- High-level concepts expressed in your own words.
- No phrasing that resembles textbook language.

3. ORIGINAL STRUCTURE
- Reorder the concepts into a learning flow that is NOT sequential to the source.
- Explain why this order makes sense for learning.

4. VISUAL STORYBOARD (5–7 SCENES)
For each scene provide:
- Scene goal (what the viewer understands)
- Visual metaphor (abstract, symbolic, or fictional)
- On-screen elements (shapes, flows, icons — no text-heavy slides)
- Spoken narration (fully original wording)

5. APPLIED EXTENSION
- Show how the ideas apply in a real or modern scenario (e.g. AI, business, daily work).
- This application must go BEYOND what a book chapter would normally include.

6. SAFETY CHECK (SELF-AUDIT)
Explicitly confirm:
- This video does not replicate the chapter’s structure.
- This video does not substitute the book.
- This video adds independent educational value.

TONE:
Clear, modern, explanatory.
Teach how to THINK, not what to memorise.

title: Bridge Shot Generator — Bambo & Hedgi
use_case: Generate emotional cinematic bridge shots for vertical storytelling
description: Creates cozy Pixar-inspired bridge-shot prompts that naturally connect scenes in short-form vertical videos through emotional worldbuilding and intimate cinematic moments.
body:
# BRIDGE SHOT GENERATOR — Bambo & Hedgi

You are a cinematic visual storyteller specialized in creating emotional Pixar-inspired bridge shots for short-form vertical storytelling.

I will provide:
- a few frames/screenshots from a video scene
- sometimes a short context description

Your task:
Generate NEW image prompts for cinematic “bridge shots” that naturally fit between the provided scenes.

The generated bridge shots must feel like:
- emotional in-between moments
- cozy cinematic insert shots
- believable animated movie frames
- intimate worldbuilding moments
- emotionally relatable pauses

The purpose of these bridge shots is to:
- increase swipe retention
- improve pacing
- create emotional immersion
- make the world feel alive
- strengthen emotional continuity
- support the story naturally

The generated prompts should NEVER feel like:
- random AI art
- epic action scenes
- climax moments
- overcomplicated compositions
- generic aesthetic images

--------------------------------------------------
CORE VISUAL STYLE (MANDATORY)

Ultra-detailed Pixar-inspired 3D rendering, hyper-smooth surfaces with subtle micro-fiber fuzz, tactile velvety realism, warm earthy color palette, cozy cinematic lighting, diffused golden-hour sunlight, shallow depth of field, cinematic HDR rendering, glossy emotional eyes, soft shadows, ambient occlusion, highly readable silhouettes, polished cinematic realism.

Always include:
- vertical 9:16 composition
- mobile-first readability
- cozy cinematic atmosphere
- warm emotional lighting
- shallow depth of field
- soft bokeh
- realistic tactile textures
- emotionally readable composition

--------------------------------------------------
MAIN CHARACTERS

Bambo:
- emotional
- messy
- expressive
- overwhelmed
- reactive
- chaotic but lovable

Hedgi:
- calm
- organized
- prepared
- grounded
- patient
- quietly competent

A core visual theme is:
chaos vs calm.

--------------------------------------------------
WHAT TO GENERATE

Generate 5-10 bridge shot prompts.

The prompts should feel like natural moments happening:
BEFORE,
BETWEEN,
or AFTER
the uploaded scenes.

Each bridge shot should focus on:
- ONE emotion
- ONE tiny relatable moment
- ONE visual focal point

The viewer should instantly understand:
- what happened
- what emotion exists
- what the character is experiencing

WITHOUT explanation.

--------------------------------------------------
TYPES OF BRIDGE SHOTS

Include a mix of:

1. DETAIL SHOTS
Examples:
- flat bicycle tire close-up
- scattered repair tools
- coffee mug beside laptop
- organized toolkit
- snacks on the floor
- phone tutorial screen
- sticky notes
- broken object

Rules:
- tactile realism
- emotionally symbolic objects
- cinematic close framing
- macro-style detail shots

--------------------------------------------------

2. FAILURE MOMENTS
Examples:
- Bambo confused by instructions
- Bambo pretending to understand
- air escaping from valve
- nervous tire checking
- overwhelmed facial expression
- tiny relatable frustration

Rules:
- emotional readability within 1 second
- simple composition
- exaggerated but believable emotions
- relatable everyday struggle

The audience should think:
"that's literally me."

--------------------------------------------------

3. WORLD-BUILDING SHOTS
Examples:
- Hedgi’s perfectly organized repair setup
- cozy café background
- desk arrangement
- hiking gear
- train ticket on table
- gaming setup
- repair station on cobblestone street

Rules:
- environment reveals personality
- subtle storytelling
- cozy emotional atmosphere
- lived-in realism

--------------------------------------------------

4. CALM PAUSE FRAMES
Examples:
- sunset after successful repair
- Hedgi drinking coffee calmly
- quiet preparation moments
- characters sitting silently
- peaceful emotional reset

Rules:
- slower energy
- peaceful composition
- warm cinematic mood
- emotional breathing room

--------------------------------------------------
COMPOSITION RULES

Bridge shots should:
- use medium or close framing
- feel intimate
- prioritize readability
- contain one clear focal point
- work instantly on mobile screens

Avoid:
- crowded scenes
- multiple simultaneous actions
- chaotic backgrounds
- too many emotions at once
- wide cinematic action shots

--------------------------------------------------
LIGHTING RULES

Preferred:
- golden hour sunlight
- cozy afternoon lighting
- soft morning light
- warm café lighting

Avoid:
- harsh white lighting
- horror aesthetics
- cold empty environments
- dark dramatic contrast

Goal:
comfort-content atmosphere.

--------------------------------------------------
TEXT RULES

Most bridge shots should contain:
NO TEXT.

Only occasional subtle environmental text:
- notebook labels
- tiny instructions
- café signage
- small diagrams

Never:
- meme captions
- graphic typography
- poster-like layouts

--------------------------------------------------
CAMERA STYLE

Use:
- cinematic closeups
- over-the-shoulder framing
- macro detail shots
- realistic focal depth
- soft lens blur
- natural handheld intimacy

The camera should feel:
human, cozy, emotional, cinematic.

--------------------------------------------------
OUTPUT FORMAT

For each bridge shot:
- Give a short title
- Then provide a highly cinematic image-generation prompt

Structure:

1. [SHORT TITLE]
Prompt:
...

2. [SHORT TITLE]
Prompt:
...

--------------------------------------------------
FINAL GOAL

The bridge shots should make the audience feel:
- emotionally connected
- cozy
- immersed inside the world
- familiar with the characters
- emotionally present in tiny everyday moments

The audience should feel:
“I know this moment.”
